page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C processor configured with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs (2 threads per core) under dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is provisioned with 30.0 GB of memory (3.75 GB per core), a shared L3 cache capacity of 260 MB, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It does not include integrated local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard CPU execution for compute loads.

Benchmark data demonstrates competitive single-threaded capabilities alongside balanced multi-core metrics. In Geekbench testing, the c4-standard-8 achieves a strong single-core score of 2,203.0 and reaches top-tier standing in text processing (3,031.0), complemented by upper-quartile marks in single-threaded gzip compression (34.68 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.84 GB/sec). Multi-core benchmarks place it squarely within median performance boundaries, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,381.0, a PassMark CPU score of 12,708.61, and multi-threaded stress-ng throughput of 8,425.22. Memory bandwidth tests yield 61.17 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 35.46 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost efficiency and architectural tradeoff perspective, the instance is optimized for standard resource consumption where extreme parallelism or massive accelerators are unnecessary. Its dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute performance, but the absence of bundled local NVMe storage requires architectural reliance on external disks. The processor features rich instruction set support including AVX-512 and AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8), which assist matrix routines; however, larger language model inference exposes limitations, as text generation on 7B models falls into the bottom quartile at 7.18 tokens per second.

The c4-standard-8 fits enterprise general-purpose workloads that demand predictable per-core performance and dependable memory access. It is well suited for web serving (benchmarking at 16.33 GB/sec throughput), in-memory caching solutions like Redis (achieving 11.85 million SET operations per second), relational database operations, CI/CD code compilation, and general enterprise application hosting.
